name: Project: a reading tracker
intro: Build a small reading tracker in stages, not one giant leap. It will store book records, total their pages, accept one new book, and make a JSON file round trip. First give the tracker its own list using a class.
prompt: Define a tracker class with __init__ receiving and storing a book list. Create an instance with at least two valid book records, then print its first book title.

name: Project: total method
intro: Add a method that totals the pages in the tracker's records. It combines a method, a list loop, dictionary lookup, a running total and return. All those pieces were introduced earlier.
prompt: Build a tracker storing a list of at least two book records. Add a no-extra-argument method that totals pages from self.books and returns the total after its loop. Print the instance method result.
why: You used project: total method in working Python.

name: Project: add a valid book
intro: Now read a title and a whole-number page count. Handle invalid number text, reject nonpositive counts with if, and append a record only on success. The sample answers are Moon and 40.
prompt: Build a tracker with a stored book list and an add method appending title/pages. Read title, then int(input()) pages in try. Catch ValueError. In else, add only if pages > 0 and print the new list length; otherwise print a helpful message.
why: You used project: add a valid book in working Python.

name: Project: a JSON file round trip
intro: Practise saving and reloading the tracker data within one program. Serialize the records, write the JSON text, reopen the same file, and decode its text. The temporary file still resets on the next Run.
prompt: Import json and create at least two book records. Write json.dumps(records) to a practice file with "w". Reopen the same file with "r", decode its read text with json.loads, then print the first restored title.
hint:
import json
books = [{"title": "Sky", "pages": 20}, {"title": "Sea", "pages": 30}]
with open("books.json", "w") as saved:
    saved.write(json.dumps(books))
with open("books.json", "r") as saved:
    restored = json.loads(saved.read())
print(restored[0]["title"])

name: Final project: your tracker
intro: Put the stages together. A tracker object stores books and provides add and total methods. Read one new book, handle conversion and positive-page validation, write and reload JSON, then list the restored books and total pages.
prompt: Combine the previous stages: import json; define a tracker class storing books, an add(title, pages) method and a returning page-total method. Start with two book records. Read title then pages, catch ValueError and add only positive pages. Write tracker records as JSON, reload into a new tracker, loop over its books to print title and pages, and print its total method result. Supply title then page text. Use the hint as a complete starting example.
